subject: Neurolytics traffic decomposition & capacity hypothesis
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Neurolytics traffic decomposition & capacity hypothesis

Alex — great talking earlier. To move quickly on a Dedicated sizing proposal we need a compact traffic breakdown from your side. Can you confirm the following items (feel free to paste numbers or attach a sample log if easier):

1) Query volume snapshot
   - DAU / MAU: approx numbers
   - Typical QPS and observed peak QPS (1h window)

2) Concurrency model
   - Active sessions (users holding an open session) vs stateless requests
   - Average session duration (minutes) and typical requests per session

3) Prompt/response token profile
   - Average prompt tokens, average response tokens, 90th/95th pctiles
   - Percentage of requests that are short (<64 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens)

4) Burst characteristics
   - Typical burst shape: sustained (minutes) or spikes (seconds)
   - Largest observed burst in past 30 days (RPS)

5) Model/quality target and fallback plan
   - Preferred model family (e.g., Llama-70B / mix of open & proprietary)
   - Whether you can accept quantized variants for lower cost

6) Latency SLO & tolerance for queuing
   - P95/P99 targets, any hard p99 SLA (ms)

7) Timeline & budget constraints

If you can attach a minute-sampled request log (CSV) or a short sample of 24‑hour token histograms that would let us produce a first-pass GPU mix and an oversubscription hypothesis. I can turn this into an initial committed capacity suggestion (reserved GPU SKUs + burst plan) for your procurement team.

Thanks — I’ll assemble a quick hypothesis and loop Marissa and Karthik for sizing.

—Dylan

Dylan — thanks for the checklist, attached is a short CSV export (minute-sampled) and a summary below. Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

Summary (past 30d):
- Product: Neurolytics conversational summarization API (text-only)
- DAU: 1,200 (power users ~120)
- Typical QPS: 6–10 sustained; observed 1-hr peak: 32 QPS; highest short spike: 78 QPS (lasting ~2m)
- Concurrency: ~480 active sessions during peak hour (session = user interactive window); average session length 9 minutes; average requests per session 5
- Token profile: avg prompt 45 tokens, avg response 300 tokens; 95th pct response ~1,100 tokens; ~14% of requests >512 tokens
- Mix: ~85% short-turn conversational requests, ~15% long-form generation
- Model target: quality equivalent to Llama-70B / preference for open models; cost-sensitivity to quantized 4-bit but we need validation on latency/quality tradeoffs
- SLO: P95 800ms for interactive queries; P99 soft target 2s but lower is preferred
- Timeline: pilot in 6 weeks; production by Q3 2028
- Budget: looking for committed commit that keeps sustained unit cost below $0.0025/token (ballpark)

Contact for engineering details: Sasha Park (sasha.park@neurolytics.ai). I uploaded the minute-sampled CSV to the Drive link below.

Best,
Alex Chen

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Neurolytics' traffic snapshot (see Alex's notes). Key numbers pulled out below and a couple of quick hypotheses; can you eyeball and give an initial Dedicated sizing recommendation and whether we should propose H100-heavy, mixed H100/A10, or A100 pool? Also flag any questions I should send back to Alex.

Pulled numbers:
- Peak short spike: 78 QPS (~2 minutes)
- 1-hr peak: 32 QPS
- Avg response tokens: 300; 95th: 1,100
- Peak active sessions: ~480 (9 min avg session, ~5 req/session)

Hypothesis (rough):
- If we target a Llama-70B-like quality using an int8/4 quantized runtime, and assume we can batch requests with small-batch continuous batching, we might need a Dedicated baseline of roughly 4-6 high-memory GPUs to cover sustained 1-hr peak with headroom and autoscale to handle the 2m spike.
- For short spikes we can rely on burst capacity (hosted overflow) + KV caching for repeated prompts to reduce token generation on hot prefixes.

Questions for sizing:
- Are we comfortable suggesting a 20–30% on-demand/hosted overflow for the short spike?
- Need to validate 95th token lengths (1,100) for P99 memory pressure — should assume worst-case for commit planning?

I attached the minute-sampled CSV link Alex provided and a one-pager token mix (neurolytics_token_mix.csv). Can you draft a 1-page capacity hypothesis and an SKU recommendation we can take to procurement?

—Dylan

Thanks for the forward, Dylan. Quick 1-page hypothesis below — happy to expand to a formal proposal.

Executive summary:
- Recommended committed capacity: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs for baseline (covers 1‑hr peak with ~20% headroom) + 2x burst H100s reserved as cold-standby for scheduled scale-ups OR mix 2xH100 + 4xA10s if Neurolytics prefers cost smoothing.

Sizing rationale:
- Sustained 1‑hr peak (32 QPS) with avg 300 tokens and quantized Llama-70B runtime: estimated steady token throughput requires ~3 H100 equiv for generation with conservative KV cache hit assumptions (20% hit). Add 1 GPU as headroom for model warmups and request variability.
- Short spike handling (78 QPS for ~2m): propose policy: autoscale to 2 burst GPUs + on-demand hosted overflow fallback for spikes above reserved burst. That keeps committed spend predictable while preserving availability.
- Memory/95th token guardrail: assume worst-case 1,100 token responses for concurrency planning — this affects model sharding and per-GPU slot counts.

Operational recommendations:
- KV prefix caching for repeated conversational prompts; aim for 30–40% cache hit on power-users to reduce tokens by ~15–20%
- Batch windows: short batching (10–30ms) plus continuous batching for small-turn chats to improve throughput without adding perceptible latency
- Canary rollout: start pilot with mixed commit (2xH100 + 2xA10) for 4 weeks, validate P95 latency against 800ms SLO, then convert to full H100 commit if quality/latency requires it

Procurement note:
- Suggested initial committed SKU: H100x4-equivalent reserved (term: 12 months) with contracted burst policy and pre-negotiated on-demand overflow. Estimated monthly committed cost to be produced by finance once we map to exact cloud SKUs.

Next steps:
- Dylan to confirm whether Neurolytics accepts 4-bit quantization for broader cost savings (we'll run an eval).
- I’ll prepare a one-page PDF proposal and an attached SKU/price mapping for procurement.
